text: Neelam Kler is an Indian neonatologist renowned for her pioneering contributions to neonatal intensive care and ventilation. She is credited with developing neonatal care that improved the survival rate of extremely preterm babies weighing less than 1000 grams to 90 percent, and reduced the infection rate to 9.8 per 1000 inpatients. The Government of India awarded her the Padmabhushan in 2014, the third-highest civilian honour, in recognition of her services to medicine and neonatology. Born in Srinagar, Jammu and Kashmir, she completed her schooling at the Presentation Convent School in Srinagar and earned a master's degree in Paediatrics from the Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences and Research (PIGMER), Chandigarh, where she also pursued further training in neonatology. She later undertook a neonatology fellowship at the Copenhagen University in Denmark. Upon returning to India, she joined Sir Ganga Ram Hospital, New Delhi, on 31 May 1988, and over a 26-year career, established and led the department of neonatology, currently serving as its Chairperson. She has also served as a visiting consultant at King Fahd University Hospital, Gizan, Saudi Arabia, and as a fellow in neonatology at Milwaukee Children's Hospital, Wisconsin, USA. Presently, she holds key positions, including being a panel member of the Newborn and Child Health Strategy of the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, and a collaborator with the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund and the World Health Organization. She chairs the Health Care at ALL Ladies League. Dr. Kler is recognized as a pioneer in intensive care and ventilation, having transformed the neonatology department at Sir Ganga Ram Hospital into a state-of-the-art facility equipped with modern high-frequency ventilation with Nitric Oxide delivery and bedside cerebral function monitoring. She has also initiated a three-year doctoral program in neonatology by the National Board of Examinations. She has published numerous articles in national and international books on paediatrics.
